messages:
Marta (Design): Shared a compact comp for export + annotation accessibility. Main questions: how do we make exported traces include annotations in a way that's both machine-searchable and SR-friendly? Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/…/trace-export-annotations

Marta (Design): Two UX constraints: 1) exported text should be searchable (plain text) 2) avoid dumping long metadata into SR focus flow when someone tabs through the exported viewer. Need suggestions.

Sam (Eng): From infra side, simplest is inline JSON with annotation objects (text, author, ts, visibility). Searchability is straightforward. For textual exports (markdown/CSV) we can append annotations after each frame as plain text prefixed with "Annotation:" so they stay searchable.

Nina (A11y): Important: in the exported HTML/preview viewer, avoid auto-announcing full annotation metadata on load. Instead provide a short line visible to SR when frame is focused: "Annotation present" and a toggle/link "Read annotation" that expands a region where the full text+meta is shown. Use aria-expanded + aria-controls.

Alex (Product): Product note: default export behavior should be conservative on privacy. Default: include team-visible annotations only; personal annotations excluded unless explicitly checked in modal. Modal copy: "Include annotations (visible in trace)" with helper: "Personal annotations are excluded by default."

Ryan (Design): Visual idea for exported markdown: keep frame line, then indented blockquote with annotation text and small italics line for metadata (author, ts). Example:

parseHeaders at line 87
> Annotation: likely missing cookie
> _marta — 2026-03-20T18:00Z_

This reads well and is searchable.

Sam (Eng): Implementation note: we should version exports (export_v2) so consumers can rely on stable fields. JSON snippet example (as string): {trace_id: "t1", frames: [{id: "f1", function: "parseHeaders", annotation: {text: "likely missing cookie", author: "marta", ts: "2026-03-20T18:00:00Z", visibility: "team"}}]}

Nina (A11y): For screen-reader users consuming the exported HTML preview, use a visually-hidden summary in each frame like: aria-label="Frame parseHeaders. Annotation available." Then a button "Read annotation" that expands the content region with role="region" and aria-live="polite" only when content changes (newly added). Don't autoplay any announcements.

Marta (Design): Good call. Also want to keep parity between in-app and exported view: if a user saw a small pill in the UI, the exported view should have a similar affordance (e.g., [Annotation] link).

Alex (Product): Also add export toggle: "Export annotations as separate file (CSV/JSON)" for programmatic consumers. Default to inline embed for human-readable formats. Add a short line: "Separate-file exports are easier to ingest by automation."

Sam (Eng): We'll implement flags: include_annotations=true, include_personal_annotations=false, export_annotations_separate=false, export_version=v2. I'll add sample CLI usage in the PR.

Ryan (Design): Accessibility microcopy: tooltip/button label should be descriptive: "Annotation — open note by Marta (team-visible)". For compact rows in exports, use icon + screen-reader-only text.

Nina (A11y): And add SR confirmation when copying annotations out of the exported viewer: "Annotation copied to clipboard." Use aria-live polite for the copy confirmation.

Marta (Design): Action items: Sam to draft export_v2 JSON + markdown templates; Nina to write the SR patterns and sample aria strings; Ryan to update Figma to include exported-view affordances; Alex to finalize modal copy and defaults. I'll consolidate and add to the spec doc.

Support-bot: Reminder: integration window 2026-04-02 02:00 UTC 1: tag PRs with #trace-export-annotations.

Marta (Design): Thanks team — I'll land the modal copy as "Include annotations (visible in trace)" and the default privacy wording unless someone objects by EOD.

Alex (Product): No objections from product. :+1:

Sam (Eng): Starting branch now, will ping when ready to demo.
